Looking at this structure, I need to analyze the secondary structure content of this 58-residue protein chain.

**Key findings from my analysis:**

**Beta sheet hydrogen bonds (long-range backbone H-bonds):**
- O(PRO2) ↔ N(ILE29) at 2.89/2.85 Å — reciprocal antiparallel pair
- O(PHE4) ↔ N(ILE27) at 2.95/2.82 Å — reciprocal antiparallel pair
- O(ALA6) → N(GLY24) at 2.78 Å and O(ASP25) → N(ALA6) at 2.82 Å
- O(SER38) ↔ N(VAL51) at 2.84/2.78 Å — reciprocal antiparallel pair
- O(GLY40) ↔ N(GLY49) at 2.65/2.96 Å — reciprocal antiparallel pair

This reveals **two 2-stranded antiparallel beta sheets**:
- Sheet 1: Strand A (residues 2-6) ↔ Strand B (residues 24-29)
- Sheet 2: Strand C (residues 37-41) ↔ Strand D (residues 47-51)

**Helix assessment:**
Careful analysis shows the H-bonds I initially identified (e.g., O(PRO52)→N(TYR55) at 2.96 Å) are actually i→i+3 contacts (3-10 helix pattern), not i→i+4 (alpha helix pattern). The i→i+4 distances are all >3.7 Å (no alpha helix H-bonds). The region 52-56 forms only a very short 3-10 helix (~4-5 residues), not a true alpha helix.

**Virtual bond angles** confirm extended conformations (angles >120°) for residues in the beta strands, consistent with beta structure.

**Summary:** ~21-25 residues in beta strands (36-43%), only ~4-5 residues in a short 3-10 helix (7-9%), no alpha helices. Beta sheet content clearly dominates over any helical content.

FINAL: predominantly beta sheet
